page: Microsoft Azure D64d_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the DDv5 server family. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8370C processor operating at 2.8 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The instance features 64 dedicated virtual CPUs mapped to 32 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It is equipped with 256.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Additionally, the server includes 2458 GB of local SSD storage, while lacking any dedicated GPU hardware.

In benchmark evaluations, the D64d_v5 demonstrates strong multi-core performance, as evidenced by high scores in multi-threaded stress-ng and Geekbench tests. Its memory subsystem shows high throughput, particularly in large-block read and write operations, reaching 291.88 GB/sec and 134.9 GB/sec respectively. Multi-threaded workloads such as bzip3 decompression, software compilation with Clang, and ray tracing also fall into the top performance tier. Conversely, single-core operations, including single-threaded gzip compression and Geekbench single-core tests, align with average performance tiers.

From a resource density perspective, the inclusion of a substantial 2458 GB local SSD alongside a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio provides high utility for data-intensive applications without requiring external storage attachments. This hardware profile is highly suited for database operations, multi-threaded data processing, large-scale software compilation, and high-throughput static web serving.
